note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: Acute shortness of breath at rest.
- Onset/duration: Began about 1 hour prior to call while sitting and watching TV; first episode.
- Progression: Not clearly worsening; patient reports feeling stressed with sensation of heart “really going.”
- Associated symptoms:
  - New, non-productive cough since yesterday.
  - Chest soreness with deep inspiration.
  - No chest pain at rest reported.
- Context:
  - Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; postpartum at home with baby.
  - No reported recent illness except frequent colds “a good few months ago.”
  - Baby well; no coughs or colds.
- Pertinent negatives/not recorded: No fever, sputum, hemoptysis, unilateral leg swelling/pain, syncope (not recorded).

Past Medical History:
- Surgical: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Chronic illnesses: Denies other medical problems.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen — reaction not recalled/unspecified.
- Medications: Codeine used regularly post-op; none taken for approximately 1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Family history: Mother had leg clots (DVT).
- Social: Postpartum, at home with baby; partner at work. Tobacco/alcohol/travel history not recorded.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth assessment; no formal vitals recorded.
- Home pulse check: Patient counted 30 beats over an unspecified interval; clinician interpreted as slightly tachycardic.
- Other exam findings: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Acute dyspnea at rest 4 weeks postpartum after C-section with palpitations and pleuritic-type chest soreness — concerning for pulmonary embolism; urgent hospital evaluation advised.
- Top plausible diagnoses (consistent with transcript and DDx):
  1) Pulmonary embolism: Postpartum status post C-section, acute SOB at rest, pleuritic discomfort, and perceived tachycardia.
  2) Viral upper respiratory infection/acute bronchitis: New cough since yesterday, but abrupt SOB at rest is less typical.
  3) Anxiety/panic-related dyspnea: Reports feeling very stressed with palpitations; does not fully explain pleuritic soreness or postpartum VTE risk.

Management Plan:
- Urgent care: Patient advised to go to the hospital promptly for evaluation of possible blood clots (VTE/PE). Ambulance was offered; patient elected self-transport with baby.
- Medication advice: Hold codeine for now.
- Safety: Go promptly and take necessary items for baby. If symptoms worsen or if unable to self-transport safely, call an ambulance.
- Education: Discussed postpartum clot risk and that hospital can provide treatment if a clot is confirmed.
- Follow-up: After hospital evaluation, follow up with primary care/OB provider as appropriate.

Patient Summary:
- 4 weeks postpartum after C-section, developed sudden shortness of breath at rest with new cough and pleuritic chest soreness. High concern for pulmonary embolism given postpartum status and symptoms. Patient is proceeding to the hospital for urgent evaluation.

Key Takeaways:
- Go to the hospital now for assessment of possible blood clots in the lungs.
- Do not take codeine for now.
- If symptoms worsen before arrival or en route, call an ambulance.

Next Steps:
- Immediate hospital evaluation for suspected VTE/PE; testing and treatment as indicated by the hospital team.
- Post-evaluation follow-up with primary care or obstetrics.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Full vital signs (SpO2, BP, temperature), ROS (fever, hemoptysis, leg swelling/pain, syncope), comprehensive medication list, obstetric details (breastfeeding status, preeclampsia, bleeding), smoking status, prior VTE history, details of ibuprofen reaction.
- Conflicts: Date of birth stated by patient as 04/20/1980; clinician repeated 1983 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Clear; no significant audio issues noted.
